synopsis: Toyota SEnS+ launched for forklifts in August 2021 and uses a rear stereo camera to distinguish people from objects [f1675, f1405, f15785]. It provides three warning levels, speed control and reverse-start prevention; reverse slowing works by cutting power, not by applying brakes to stop the forklift [f1406, f1676, f1407, f15786]. The Toyota and Linde forklift precedents report validation of pedestrian-versus-object detection with internal evidence acceptance, but published validation methods were unavailable [f1890, f1893, f1891]. The research also found no Toyota operating conditions, capability-building or validation durations, remaining physical-testing requirements, or safety case quantifying reduced physical testing, limiting their usefulness for planning validation effort [f1679, f1892, f1894]. The glossary additionally records that field problems were not found; this is an evidence gap, not evidence that none occurred [f15788].
